lessons.title: Freedom date = leftover + the book
lessons.keyIdea: A date here needs leftover and the book. Missing either means the date is unknown — never invented.
paragraphs: A Freedom date here comes from leftover and the book. Leftover is one-time cash from Budget, not leftover times 12. The book is what Invest shows you own.
If leftover or the book is missing, the date is unknown. This page will not invent a year. Journey Home says the same thing: needs leftover and a book.
Spending in the plan is a later assumption. First, leftover and the book have to exist in the tools. If this lesson and a screen disagree, the tools win.

cta.label: Open Freedom and see what it has

checks.prompt: A Freedom date here comes from…
If leftover or the book is missing…

lessons.title: Spending is an assumption until you save a plan
lessons.keyIdea: Spending is what you type and save. It is not leftover, and this page will not invent a lifestyle.
paragraphs: A Freedom plan needs a spending number to draw a path. Until you save a plan, that number is an assumption, not a fact from your accounts.
The tool will not pull a lifestyle from leftover. Leftover is leftover. Spending is what you type and save. Treat any spending on screen as the plan’s assumption — not a number this lesson invents.
Save a plan when you are ready to pick a spending number you can live with. You can change it later. Do not copy a sample year from this page.

cta.label: Open Freedom and save a plan

lessons.title: Inflation in one page
lessons.keyIdea: Inflation means prices rise. The rate in use is whatever the saved plan shows — not a rate from this lesson.
paragraphs: Inflation means prices rise over time. The same basket of goods can cost more next year. A plan that ignores that can look easier than life will be.
Freedom can use an inflation rate as an assumption. It is a setting, not a forecast we promise. This lesson does not invent a rate for you. Check the plan for the rate in use.
You cannot stop inflation from a lesson. You can only see that a path in today’s dollars and a path in future dollars are different stories. The saved plan is the source.

lessons.title: The chart is a story, not a promise
lessons.keyIdea: The chart is a path from leftover, the book, and saved assumptions. Paths can miss. You can lose money.
paragraphs: The Freedom chart is a path the tool drew from leftover, the book, and the assumptions you saved. Paths can miss. Markets can fall. You can lose money.
A crossing year is not a guarantee you can stop working. If leftover or the book changes, the story changes. If leftover or the book is missing, there is no honest date to show.
Read the chart as “what this plan says if these inputs hold.” Then go back to Budget and Invest and check the inputs. The tools are the source.
